tools.name: explain_stock
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one company or ticker in general: 'tell me about X', 'what does X do', 'how is X doing', 'explain X stock', its price, chart or business. Shows invest-like's stock page in a card: price and one-year chart, one plain sentence, four checks with the numbers behind them

tools.name: check_value
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether a stock is a good buy, a good investment, worth buying, undervalued, overvalued, cheap, expensive, or worth it at today's price. tools.name: compare_stocks
tools.description: Use this when the user names 2 to 4 stocks and asks which is better, to compare them, or writes 'X or Y' / 'X vs Y' (e.g. 'Visa or Mastercard?', 'Apple vs Microsoft'). Shows them side by side: the four plain checks (profit, growth, price, debt), sales growth, net margin, return on capital, P/E, debt

tools.name: score_portfolio
tools.description: Use this when the user shares the stocks or funds they own (a portfolio, holdings, 'my stocks', a broker list) and wants to know how it looks, a score, or what to watch. Takes up to 60 holdings, each a ticker or company name with optional shares or money amount. Returns invest-like's portfolio score

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "compare_stocks" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Use this when the user names 2 to 4 stocks and asks which is better, to compare them, or writes 'X or Y' / 'X vs Y' (e.g. 'Visa or Mastercard?', 'Apple vs Microsoft'). Shows them side by side: the four plain checks (profit, growth, price, debt), sales growth, net margin, return on capital, P/E, debt" → after: "Use this when the user names 2 to 4 stocks and asks which is better, to compare them, or writes 'X or Y' / 'X vs Y' (e.g. 'Visa or Mastercard?', 'Apple vs Microsoft'). Shows them side by side: the four plain checks (profit, growth, price, debt), sales growth, net margin, return on capital, P/E, debt"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
